newsitem.title: USA: US Senate panel oks $200 mln SPR oil sale.
newsitem.headline: US Senate panel oks $200 mln SPR oil sale.

text.p: A U.S. Senate Appropriations subcommittee on Friday passed an Interior spending bill that would sell more than $200 million of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve next year.
Subcommittee Chairman Slade Gorton, a Washington Republican, said tight money "made it impossible to avoid another oil sale."
The House earlier this week in its $13 billion Interior spending bill approved a $209 million SPR oil sale to cover next year's operating costs for the reserve.

The Senate subcommittee also approved its version of the $13 billion measure to fund next year's programs for federal lands, Native Americans, energy research and security, minerals management and cultural programs.

Unlike the House bill, the Senate panel's bill provided $100 million for the National Endowment for the Arts. It also would use $700 million for federal land acquisition, including purchases to halt a mine development near Yellowstone National Park and to protect the Headwaters old growth forest in California.
